content:
mike: quick heads-up — ran a smoke compare between rerank-v3 (fp16) and rerank-v3-int8 on the standard holdout, weird split: NDCG@10 up but MRR down. unsure if this is real or a harness mismatch.

jana: can you paste the numbers?

mike: sure — baseline (fp16): NDCG@10=0.672, MRR@10=0.411; int8: NDCG@10=0.689, MRR@10=0.387. Ran against holdout-2026-02, seed=42, topk=100.

eli: interesting. magnitude is small but consistent?

mike: ran 3 seeds, same trend each time. variance small (~0.003).

jana: my first guess is candidate curation or preproc differences between offline eval harness and prod candidate pipeline. we recently changed snippet extraction for SERP (html_strip -> keep-snippets).

tara: also check tokenizer parity — our quant runtime uses a slightly different tokenizer config (strip_accents=false) for perf. that can shift token boundaries and impact MRR more than NDCG.

samir: could priming length / prefix tokens cause NDCG to go up (favoring rank distribution) while top-1 MRR falls? e.g., int8 calibration might prefer slightly different score spread.

jana: agreed. we should aim to isolate factors in small ablations. propose 3 reproductions: unified-candidates (use prod candidate generator), tokenizer-parity (force tokenization in harness to match runtime), and priming-parity (apply same query priming/truncation).

mike: plan sounds good. i can run unified-candidates + tokenizer-parity today. will need generator snapshot id. @jana do you have the latest candidate snapshot id for holdout-2026-02?

jana: snapshot id: cs-2026-02-1487. use candidate-filter:v2 (dedupe+hosted-url-normalize).

eli: small note — when you run, include these flags so we can track:
```
./eval_runner \
  --model rerank-v3-int8 \
  --holdout holdout-2026-02 \
  --seed 42,43,44 \
  --candidates cs-2026-02-1487 \
  --tokenizer-config prod-tokenizer.json \
  --priming-config prod-priming.json \
  --out run_outputs/3300001111.json
```

mike: copying that to my shell. quick sanity log i saw this morning (before candidate parity):
```
[RUN] model=rerank-v3-int8 seed=42 NDCG@10=0.689 MRR@10=0.387 p@1=0.282
[RUN] model=rerank-v3-fp16 seed=42 NDCG@10=0.672 MRR@10=0.411 p@1=0.301
```

jana: big gap in p@1 — that screams tokenization or candidate normalization to me. NDCG is more tolerant.

samir: we should also check candidate overlap rate between pools. if int8 variant is better at reordering tail but worse at exact top-1, overlap metrics will show it.

tara: i'll run a quick overlap diff tool: `python tools/candidate_overlap.py --a cs-2026-02-1487 --b eval-candidates-temp` and post results.

dev-bot: scheduled job eval-3300001111-unified for 3300001111 by mike — status: queued.

mike: dev-bot thanks. i'll kick off the three ablations in this order: 1) unified-candidates+prod-tokenizer, 2) prod-priming only, 3) unified all parity. will report back with the minimal change that flips MRR.

eli: +1. also include a small binary: compute NDCG@1/3/10 and MRR@1/5/10, plus topk overlap and tokenization-shift stats (fraction of queries where token count changed).

jana: reminder: when you do tokenizer parity, please set `lowercase=false` and `strip_html=true` to match prod. dev harness defaults to lowercase=true historically. that can move exact-match top1.

mike: noted. running now. ETA ~2h for seeds across cluster.

(dev-bot)  — job eval-3300001111-unified started on runner-gpu-12

mike: quick interim — overlap tool shows 98.6% overlap between cs-2026-02-1487 and eval-candidates-temp, but 1.4% of queries had different top-1 id after dedupe normalization.

samir: that 1.4% could explain a decent chunk of p@1/MRR delta. are those high-traffic queries or longtail?

jana: sampling shows they're longtail but heavier for brand queries (exact URL matches). product team changed URL normalization last month.

mike: run results (ablation 1: unified candidates + prod-tokenizer):
```
ablation1 (unified+cand + prod-tokenizer) seeds=42,43,44
avg NDCG@10=0.687 (+0.015 vs fp16)
avg MRR@10=0.405 (-0.006 vs fp16)
avg p@1=0.297 (-0.004)
```

eli: that's helpful — MRR gap reduced but still exists. suggests priming/truncation might be remaining factor.

tara: ablation 2 (prod-priming only) planned next?

mike: yes. queuing. dev-bot scheduled eval-3300001111-priming.

(dev-bot) job eval-3300001111-priming queued by mike.

mike: after priming parity:
```
ablation2 (prod-priming only) avg NDCG@10=0.675 avg MRR@10=0.398 p@1=0.293
```

samir: ok priming moves MRR a bit. combined parity next should get us close to fp16 numbers.

jana: once we have combined run, let's also run a tiny online A/B on 1% traffic with int8 + fallback to fp16 for mismatched top1 for 1 minute windows — so we can measure actual user-visible relevance changes. need product + infra signoff though.

mike: running ablation3 (full parity).

(dev-bot) job eval-3300001111-fullparity started.

mike: final combined run finished:
```
full parity (candidates+tokenizer+priming) avg NDCG@10=0.686 avg MRR@10=0.409 p@1=0.300
```

eli: that basically closes the gap. looks like the earlier signal was harness / candidate normalization mismatches plus a small priming delta. int8 itself isn't catastrophically harming MRR.

jana: good find. action items:
- mike: open PR to add prod-tokenizer and prod-priming fixtures to eval harness (so future compares default to parity)
- tara: add candidate snapshot id to eval meta so we always record pool version
- samir: run a short 1% A/B with fallback policy and guardrails (metrics: p@1, MRR@10, error rate)

mike: will open PR with run commands and logs. attaching run outputs to ticket INF-4367.

dev-bot: ticket INF-4367 updated with artifacts: run_outputs/3300001111.json

samir: thanks everyone. learned: small infra/preproc differences can flip top-1 more than bulk metrics. add tests. :white_check_mark:

jana: adding harness test that runs tokenization parity check for new model uploads.

mike: closing loop here. ping me if you want the raw runs.

(ends)
